cards.back:
Near-future plans, intentions, and scheduled actions. Equivalent to English 'going to + verb.'

'We are going to launch tomorrow.'
→ Vamos a lanzar mañana.
cards.grammarNote: *Ir a + infinitive* is the most common way to talk about the near future in spoken Spanish. It is more frequent than the simple future tense in everyday conversation.

cards.back:
yo → voy
tú → vas
él/ella → va
nosotros → vamos
vosotros → vais
ellos/ellas → van
cards.grammarNote: *Ir* is completely irregular in the present tense — must be memorized. The *a* (to) always follows before the infinitive.

cards.front: I am going to review your code after lunch.
cards.back: Voy a revisar tu código después del almuerzo.
cards.grammarNote:
*Voy a* = I am going to (first person singular).
*Después del almuerzo* = after lunch; *del* = contraction of *de + el*.

cards.front: Are you going to finish the feature today?
cards.grammarNote: *Vas a* = you are going to (informal tú). In questions, the word order stays the same as statements — only intonation (and ¿?) changes.

cards.front: The server is going to crash if we don't fix this.
cards.back: El servidor va a caerse si no arreglamos esto.
cards.grammarNote:
*Va a caerse* = is going to crash/fall; *caerse* = reflexive infinitive (to fall/crash).
*Si no arreglamos* = if we don't fix; present tense after *si* in real conditional sentences.

cards.front: We are going to launch the new version tomorrow.
cards.back: Vamos a lanzar la nueva versión mañana.
cards.grammarNote: *Vamos a* = we are going to (first person plural). Also used as a command/suggestion: *¡Vamos a trabajar!* = 'Let's work!'

cards.front: They are going to review the pull requests this afternoon.
cards.back: Van a revisar los pull requests esta tarde.
cards.grammarNote:
*Van a* = they are going to (third person plural).
*Esta tarde* = this afternoon; *esta* is feminine to agree with *tarde* (afternoon, feminine).

cards.front: Jeffrey is going to deploy the code before the deadline.
cards.back: Jeffrey va a desplegar el código antes de la fecha límite.
cards.grammarNote:
*Va a desplegar* = he is going to deploy; third person singular.
*Antes de la fecha límite* = before the deadline — a key phrase in every sprint.

cards.front: We are going to have an emergency meeting.
cards.back: Vamos a tener una reunión de emergencia.
cards.grammarNote:
*Vamos a tener* = we are going to have; *tener* as infinitive after *vamos a*.
*De emergencia* = emergency (adjective phrase modifying *reunión*).

cards.front: I am not going to be able to finish before Friday.
cards.back: No voy a poder terminar antes del viernes.
cards.grammarNote:
*No voy a poder* = I am not going to be able to; *poder* as infinitive after *no voy a*.
*Antes del viernes* = before Friday; *del* = *de + el*.

cards.front: What are you going to do about the bug?
cards.back: ¿Qué vas a hacer con el bug?
cards.grammarNote:
*¿Qué vas a hacer?* = What are you going to do? *Hacer* = infinitive (to do).
*Con el bug* = with the bug / about the bug — *con* (with) can translate as 'about' in this context.

cards.front: Jeffrey says in the standup: 'Today I am going to work on the new feature.'
cards.back: Jeffrey dice en el standup: 'Hoy voy a trabajar en la nueva función.'
cards.grammarNote:
*Hoy voy a* = today I am going to; time expression *hoy* reinforces the near-future meaning.
*Trabajar en* = to work on; *en* is the correct preposition here, not *a*.

cards.front: What is the difference between 'voy a lanzar' and 'lanzaré'?
cards.back:
*Voy a lanzar* = I am going to launch (near future, planned, conversational)
*Lanzaré* = I will launch (simple future, more formal or distant future)
cards.grammarNote: In everyday spoken Spanish, *ir a + infinitive* is preferred over the simple future for near-term plans. The simple future is common in formal writing and for distant or hypothetical events.

cards.front: Careful — this is going to delete all the data.
cards.back: Cuidado — esto va a borrar todos los datos.
cards.grammarNote:
*Cuidado* = 'careful / watch out' — fixed exclamation.
*Va a borrar* = is going to delete/erase; third person singular of *borrar* (to delete/erase).

cards.front: This week we are going to close all the open tickets.
cards.back: Esta semana vamos a cerrar todos los tickets abiertos.
cards.grammarNote:
*Esta semana* = this week; time expressions often go at the start for emphasis.
*Abiertos* = open (adjective); masculine plural to agree with *tickets*.
